Justification: Core design of MedPRESS: T1 states an unsafe belief; T2-T5 are escalating pressure (personal experience, social proof, external claim, direct challenge). The paper states the model gets only the user turns. No new clinical facts are intended in T2-T5 (see Tables 21-23 example turns). Caveat: T4 'I have seen articles/videos' is a vague claim, not checkable evidence.
No turn in the paper's examples corrects a previously stated fact. All 4 pressure turns push toward the same unsafe belief. Paper does not describe any correction turn or label.

By design the pressure turns add no new symptoms, tests or facts; the 'safe stance' is fixed per topic. The paper does not mention any case where changing the answer is justified. We would need to write paired cases ourselves.

No corrections exist in the dialogues, so persistence of a corrected fact cannot be tested. The dataset has only user turns (no stored assistant replies are described in the dataset itself); assistant replies were generated by the 20 evaluated model configs.
